thread.title: Micron Technology Picked Up The Pieces From Samsung's Poor Q4 Guidance - Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) | Seeking Alpha

author: Robert Castellano
title: Micron Technology Picked Up The Pieces From Samsung's Poor Q4 Guidance - Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) | Seeking Alpha
text:
Samsung Electronics ( OTC:SSNLF ), in its recent preliminary Q4 guidance, disclosed that its operating profits should drop by 38.5% QoQ to 10.8 trillion won in the past three months, from 15.1 trillion, primarily on weakening market demand for memory chips, the biggest source of its profits. The operating profits would fall far short of the market expectations of -10% to 13.6 trillion won. According to the filing, weak memory chip sales and escalating market uncertainties were to blame for its lower-than-expected earnings.
What happened? First, Apple ( AAPL ) is Samsung's biggest customer for memory chips and smartphone screens. The previous week, Apple gave preliminary guidance for the previous quarter, reducing its sales forecast and blaming slowing iPhone sales in China and lingering uncertainty over US-China trade relations. Second, there were sluggish sales to U.S. cloud server companies. Third, there is a slowdown in PC DRAM sales as well as concern of a slowdown in the global economy. Finally, Samsung had sales pull-ins in Q3, which artificially inflated revenues compared to its peers.
Two caveats for the reader - competitiveness combined with collusion First, it must be remembered that the memory market is extremely competitive. I discussed in an August 2, 2018, Seeking Alpha article entitled "Semiconductor Memory Companies Are Actually Competitors Of Each Other Not Allies." I noted in the bullets that:
Memory companies have benefited over the past 18 months from high demand and low supply. NAND prices are dropping, and DRAM prices should start in the next few quarters, signifying that we may be reaching a small oversupply situation. In the past, positive earnings of one company would signify that all companies would exhibit positive results. With an oversupply, that is changing. Recent positive earnings from SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics resulted in a bounce in stock of Micron Technology ( MU ). In the new paradigm, these memory companies need to be considered by investors as competitors, not allies. Readers should recognize that on August 2 when this article appeared, and I warned of DRAM prices dropping, MU stock closed at $53.30. At that time, MU longs were in denial that the stock would continue rising based on erroneous forecasts by some analysts that the stock would reach $100 and also benefit from $10 billion in buybacks, both of which were wrong. Of the 90 comments, I received only two likes.
Second, it must be remembered that in the DRAM sector, these two companies plus SK Hynix ( OTC:HXSCL ), function as an oligopoly, utilizing tacit collusion to control output to eliminate cutthroat competition. My arguments were presented in a December 17, 2018, Seeking Alpha article entitled "If Micron Is Part Of A DRAM Oligopoly, Why Is The Stock Down 55% From A High In May?"
On December 17, MU stock closed at $33.88., down 36.4% from its price on August 2. Perhaps the mentality of the MU longs changed as they came to realize that my negative comments about the memory sector may have sunk in, because of 206 comments for the article, I got 26 likes.
Samsung's loss is Micron's gain Micron Technology announced its quarterly earnings for its end-November 1Q FY2019. Group revenues rose 16% to $7.91 billion but missed analysts' forecasts of $8.02 billion. Since MU's quarter ended in November and Samsung's quarter ended in December, financial data offer a good comparative of the performance of the two companies.
Recognizing that tacit collusion can only do so much without drawing the attention and ire of Chinese government officials or the possibility of further class action lawsuits, I want to focus on the competitive nature of the memory market as illustrated by these two companies.
But the reader must recognize that my thesis is based on the fact that, on a macro level, we are not witnessing a global recession that may have given rise to Samsung's poor preliminary Q4 results or Micron's dismal Q2 FY2019 guidance. Instead, as I indicated above, relating to the reasons for Samsung's results, the Apple or cloud server providers are micro-based. Yes, the trade issues with China are taking their toll at a macro level, but I don't see it long term.

Investor Takeaway Micron Technology has shown significantly better performance over the past several months than competitor Samsung Electronics. Investors need to recognize that these companies are discrete entities and should be evaluated on an individual basis.
Unfortunately, the Street doesn't think that way. As of this writing on January 9, MU stock is up more than 6% because of an upgrade by Bernstein and an agreement by MU with Qualcomm ( QCOM ) for infotainment systems in next-gen vehicles and Intel's ( INTC ) Mobileye for the development of its fifth-gen autonomous driving platform.
In tandem, Samsung Electronics stock closed up 3.94% on January 9, despite the company's poor preliminary guidance for Q4. SK Hynix stock closed up 7.43% on January 9 even with no news coming out of the company.
Nevertheless, the strong performance of MU in the face of huge capex spends by Samsung in 2018 illustrates the company is on the right path as far as adjusting inventory, capex spend, and technology improvements.
